Capture (1:33): Immediately offload ideas, tasks, notes, or media onto an external platform (e.g., app, notebook) as quickly as possible. This step is crucial because capturing and organizing are useless if the information is never revisited (5:27). The speaker recommends scheduling dedicated review sessions, such as three 30-minute blocks daily (5:50). During review, captured items are transformed into concrete commitments or actions, like blocking time on a calendar or adding topics to meeting notes (6:04). Engage (2:32): Execute the work or act on the processed information (6:40). This closes the loop of the workflow, turning a captured item into a completed action (2:36).

*CORE Productivity Workflow: Capture → Organize → Review → Engage.* >Capture: Get tasks & ideas out of your head immediately. >Organize: Tag, set due dates, or sort for easy access. >Review: Check your inboxes regularly and turn ideas into concrete actions. >Engage: Do the work during focused blocks.

The inability to edit or animate splats makes them useless for anything but static environments. Plus, it can take many hours (20 hours for the sewer scene on my channel) running a high-end GPU to produce a big splat. Further, that completed splat has no capacity for physics, which is quickly becoming the foremost consideration for machine generated assets. Without embedded data for physics you can't use splats for anything but background scenery.
